work.title: Work
work.lead: If you only read one entry, read the first. The rest shows how I got there.

cto.text: Overall responsibility for strategy, development, and operations of the marketplace and ERP platform. Next.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Turborepo, Railway, Cloudflare. Commission models and payouts stay configurable, so a new market does not require a code change.

ecommerce.text: Product responsibility for the online shops: roadmap, Shopify, and the connections to warehouse and customer service.

engineer.text: An Angular 19 application in an Nx monorepo, UI from Figma with Tailwind, and interfaces over OpenAPI and RxJS.

projects.title: Projects
projects.lead: Reading about it is one thing. Here are three things you can click: the store I run today, Wire's source, and the thesis code.
projects.note: Wire fetches sources, keeps an index, and asks Jev one yes/no question. The repository is public.

wire.where: Python · Qdrant · Jev · one process, many desks
wire.text: Wire reads a set of sources on a schedule, keeps an index, and asks Jev one yes/no question about every new story. Which sources, how often, which question — that is a desk.

events.text: The backend from my thesis: an event manager with staff, lines, business units, feedback and votes. Written in 2023 entirely by prompting chat-based AI models — the experiment the thesis is about. Archived unchanged.

smartport.text: The marketplace I run as CTO: storefront, seller payouts, search, shipping and compliance on one platform. Not a demo — this is the shop that takes orders.

education.title: Education
education.lead: Two lines. The thesis is the interesting one if you work with AI in the browser.
education.text: Bachelor's examination on 19 December 2023. The thesis at Randstad Digital looks at what chat-based AI models can carry in web development, and where they stop.

offer.meta: AI consulting for small businesses in Rhine-Main | Robin Prause
offer.description: Less office work for small businesses in Frankfurt and Rhine-Main. I come along, find what eats your time and set up AI tools you can run yourself.
offer.kicker: CTO know-how and AI for small businesses · Rhine-Main
offer.claim: More time for what you actually started out to do.
offer.lede: Quotes on Sunday, emails after hours? I find the work that takes the most time and set it up so it runs on the side.
offer.ctaHint: No obligation. The list is yours, even without a job.

steps.title: How it works
steps.lead: No risk at the start, no dependency at the end.

one.title: I come along
one.text: I watch the work and ask questions. Not to check on anyone, but to see where the time goes. Afterwards you get a short list. It is yours, even if you don't hire me.

two.title: One task, one fixed price
two.text: I propose the one piece of work that relieves you the most and name a fixed sum up front. No timesheets, no surprises on the invoice.

three.title: Set up and practise
three.text: I set it up with tools that run in your name and practise it with the people who do the work. Until it no longer feels new.

four.title: Handover
four.text: Once you can do it on your own, I leave. No subscription, no dependency. What stays is the time you get back.

tasks.title: What piles up
tasks.lead: Small things that cost a few minutes every day and add up to weeks over a year. I see what it is for you when I come along.

quotes.title: Quotes and invoices
quotes.text: Notes, photos or a phone call turn into a finished draft. You check it and send it, instead of spending Sunday at the desk.

mail.title: Inbox
mail.text: Requests are sorted, standard questions already have a draft reply. No customer waits because an email got lost.

reports.title: Reports from the field
reports.text: Whoever works outside speaks briefly into their phone. A finished report is waiting at the office, no typing in the evening.

paper.title: Appointments and paperwork
paper.text: Scheduling appointments, understanding letters from authorities, keeping deadlines in view. Less to keep turning over in your head.

private.title: For you, privately
private.text: Your own inbox, your paperwork, or a smart home you maintain yourself afterwards. So your evening is yours again.

why.title: Why me
why.lead: Technology is changing every week right now. I follow it every day and bring you the part that actually helps in your daily work.

overview.title: I keep track, so you don't have to
overview.text: As a CTO I am responsible for the technology of a whole platform and decide every week which new tools are worth it and which are just noise. I bring that knowledge to you, translated into your daily work and without jargon.

care.title: For the people, not past them
care.text: This is not about replacing anyone. It is about your people typing and searching less and doing more of the work they are good at and enjoy.

self.title: The one who comes along also sets it up
self.text: No sales team, no agency, no interns. I come along, set it up, hand it over and explain everything without jargon. You have one contact from start to finish.

ai.title: I know where AI stops
ai.text: My bachelor's thesis in 2023 tested what chat-based AI can really do and where it fails. I have worked with it every day since. That is why I only propose what runs reliably for you.

tech.title: I know what counts in day-to-day operations
tech.text: I have built and run platforms with payments, shipping and compliance that handle real orders every day. I know where data goes and what has to happen so nothing gets lost.

near.title: I come to you
near.text: I live in Rodgau near Frankfurt. Coming along and practising happen at your place, not on a video call.

fit.title: Who it is for
fit.lead: For businesses where everyone already has enough on their plate.

yes.title: Small businesses under 20 people
yes.text: No IT of their own, and the owner decides. For example landscaping, waste and composting, farming or service businesses.

also.title: Freelancers and private people
also.text: When it is about one clear task you carry on with yourself afterwards.

no.title: Ongoing support
no.text: If you are looking for someone who is always on call or fills a position, I am the wrong person.

band.title: Sounds like your week?
band.text: Two or three sentences are enough. I reply personally and we see if it fits.

faq.title: Questions
faq.lead: What you probably want to know before you let me into your business.

day.q: Why come along instead of just asking?
day.a: In a conversation people tell you what comes to mind. When I am there, I see what really costs time. You get the list either way, even without a job.

jobs.q: Will my people worry about their jobs?
jobs.a: That is not what this is about. I take away work nobody likes doing, so there is more time for the work that matters. When I come along, I tell the team exactly that.

which.q: Will you see the right work?
which.a: We pick a time when the most piles up. Whatever only comes up once a month, such as billing, we go through briefly together.

trade.a: True. That is why I come along instead of showing slides. You know your trade. I bring the overview of technology I have built up as a CTO and explain it so it fits you.

worth.q: How do I know it was worth it?
worth.a: Beforehand we write down how long the task takes today. After the handover we check how long it takes now.

ai.q: Do I need to know about AI?
ai.a: No. You only need to know which work is a pain. Whether and which AI is behind it is my job.

after.q: What if something stops working later?
after.a: I only set up what you can change and fix yourselves, and I show you how at the handover. After that I am no longer involved.

data.a: With you. Every account runs in your name, and the provider bills you directly. I don't resell software.

price.a: A fixed sum for exactly one task. I name it after I have come along, before I start.

offer.foot: Tell me in two or three sentences what piles up for you. I will reply personally.

privacy.description: What happens to personal data on this site.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What happens to personal data on this site. If the English and German texts ever differ, the German text applies.
privacy.host: The site is hosted by Render Services, Inc., United States, on a server in Frankfurt am Main. Render processes data so the site can be delivered. Because Render is based in the United States, access from there can happen. That rests on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or, where that does not apply, on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.
privacy.logs: When a page is opened, the server processes the IP address, date and time, the address requested, the browser identifier, and the status of the response. This is needed to deliver the page and to keep the service secure. It is not used for advertising, and it is not built into a profile. The legal basis is Article 6 (1) (f) GDPR: a working and secure site. The host keeps these logs for its operational period. This site does not keep a log archive of its own.
privacy.storageTitle: Cookies and storage on your device
privacy.storage: This site sets no cookies. There is no analytics and no advertising. Fonts are loaded from this site, not from another provider. If you choose Light or Dark, that choice is stored on your device under the name prause-theme. The reading depth is stored for the browser tab under the name prause-depth and is dropped when the tab closes. The legal basis is section 25 (2) TDDDG: the storage exists for a setting you switch on yourself.
privacy.mail: The form sends your name, email address, and message to mail@robin-prause.de. This site does not store the message. It passes through the Render server in Frankfurt to the Hostinger mailbox, where it stays until I delete it. The basis is Article 6 (1) (b) GDPR when you ask about working together, otherwise Article 6 (1) (f) GDPR so I can answer. The mail link next to the form still opens your own mail program.
privacy.rights: You can ask for access, correction, deletion and restriction, and you can object to processing that rests on legitimate interest. You can also lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
privacy.authority: The Hessian Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information, Gustav-Stresemann-Ring 1, 65189 Wiesbaden.
